title: HDFC Bank Board Fines CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan Over Deposit Pricing Overreach
excerpt: India's largest private lender concludes its internal review of the MSRDC deposit arrangement, finding business overreach but no misconduct or personal enrichment.
body:
• HDFC Bank's board has fined CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan, CFO Srinivasan Vaidyanathan, and Group Head Arvind Vohra ₹1 lakh each over deposit arrangements with the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation.
  • A Special Disciplinary Committee of Independent Directors found the conduct amounted to business overreach — not misconduct, personal enrichment, or improper motive.
  • The board directed that the matter be communicated to the Reserve Bank of India, formally closing the internal disciplinary process.
  • The penalty comes amid broader scrutiny of Jagdishan, who separately faces fraud allegations from the Lilavati Trust that HDFC Bank has called baseless and retaliatory.

The MSRDC Deposit Review

HDFC Bank on Monday concluded an internal review that had hung over its top leadership for months. The bank's board, meeting on July 23, determined that its CEO, CFO, and a senior retail assets executive had engaged in business overreach in their handling of deposit arrangements with the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) in 2017 and 2021.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=JF3FPpR-Uuc

"HDFC Bank has categorically denied the allegations, calling them "baseless and malicious" and characterising the legal action as retaliatory."

A Special Disciplinary Committee of Independent Directors examined the arrangements and found that the employees' conduct "constituted business overreach rather than any mala fide action, personal enrichment, or improper motive," the bank said in a regulatory filing.

The board issued warning letters and imposed a monetary penalty of ₹1 lakh each on Managing Director and CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan, Chief Financial Officer Srinivasan Vaidyanathan, and Group Head – Retail Assets Arvind Vohra. Remaining employees associated with the matter received warning letters without financial penalties.

RBI Implications

While clearing the executives of misconduct, the board acknowledged a "potential divergence with the applicable RBI Directions" — a carefully worded signal that the deposit pricing may not have fully complied with Reserve Bank guidelines. The board directed that the outcome be communicated to the RBI, formally closing the bank's internal process.

The distinction between overreach and misconduct matters significantly for Jagdishan's position. Had the committee found deliberate wrongdoing or personal enrichment, the consequences would have been far more severe, potentially triggering RBI intervention in the bank's leadership.

A CEO Under Multiple Pressures

The MSRDC disciplinary action arrives at a complicated moment for Jagdishan. In a separate and unrelated matter, the Lilavati Kirtilal Mehta Medical Trust — which operates Mumbai's Lilavati Hospital — filed an FIR against the HDFC Bank CEO earlier this year, alleging that he accepted a ₹2.05 crore bribe to help the Chetan Mehta Group retain illegal control over the Trust.

HDFC Bank has categorically denied the allegations, calling them "baseless and malicious" and characterising the legal action as retaliatory. The bank says the Trust's Mehta family defaulted on loans from a consortium that HDFC Bank was part of, and that the fraud allegations are a deliberate attempt to obstruct recovery proceedings for ₹65.22 crore in outstanding dues. Jagdishan has moved the Bombay High Court seeking to quash the FIR.

What It Means for Investors

The ₹1 lakh penalty is symbolic — roughly $120 — but the governance signal is what matters. The board's decision to investigate, convene an independent committee, and publicly disclose the findings demonstrates institutional checks at India's largest private lender, which holds over ₹27 lakh crore in assets. For NRI investors with significant exposure to HDFC Bank through direct holdings or mutual funds, the resolution removes one source of uncertainty around the bank's leadership stability.
